capability.conversionCommand: qemu-img convert -p -O qcow2 '/Users/example/Virtual Machines/Veil/Windows 11 Arm.img' '/Users/example/Virtual Machines/Veil/Windows 11 Arm.qcow2'
capability.detail: This Windows system disk is raw, and QEMU internal snapshots can only be stored inside a qcow2 image. Disks Veil creates now are qcow2; older ones are raw. Suspend and resume still work on this disk because they stream guest memory to a separate file.

nextActions: This Windows system disk is raw, and QEMU internal snapshots can only be stored inside a qcow2 image. Disks Veil creates now are qcow2; older ones are raw. Suspend and resume still work on this disk because they stream guest memory to a separate file.

Shut down Windows and choose Configuration > Disk > Convert to qcow2, which converts the disk, switches the VM to /Users/example/Virtual Machines/Veil/Windows 11 Arm.qcow2, and moves the raw file to the Trash.
The equivalent manual command is: qemu-img convert -p -O qcow2 '/Users/example/Virtual Machines/Veil/Windows 11 Arm.img' '/Users/example/Virtual Machines/Veil/Windows 11 Arm.qcow2'
Use veil-vmctl vm-suspend --json when you only need to keep the current Windows session, which works on the current disk format.
